title: Mobile UX & Mobile-First Design
description: Design responsive, mobile-first mobile app experiences that respect platform guidelines. Tests iOS/Android patterns, touch target sizing, and mobile gesture design.

seo.overviewTitle: Mobile UX Design (iOS HIG & Android Material 3)
seo.overviewBody: Mobile UX design accounts for touch ergonomics, limited screen real estate, and platform conventions. Product designers prove readiness by designing mobile-first layouts, adhering to Apple HIG vs Android Material 3 guidelines, and optimizing for thumb-zone accessibility.

deliverables.title: 1. iOS & Android Mobile App UI Design Deck
deliverables.desc: Mobile app screen designs tailored to platform conventions (iOS navigation bars vs Android bottom navigation).

deliverables.title: 2. Thumb Zone Ergonomics & Navigation Audit
deliverables.desc: Ergonomic audit mapping key interactive UI elements within natural thumb reach zones.

deliverables.title: 3. Mobile Touch Target & Gesture Specification
deliverables.desc: Specification establishing minimum 44x44pt touch targets, pull-to-refresh gestures, and swipe actions.

faqs.question: What are the primary differences between iOS HIG and Android Material 3?
faqs.answer: iOS uses centered navigation titles, back chevrons, and SF Pro typography. Android Material 3 uses left-aligned titles, floating action buttons (FAB), Material icons, and Roboto/Variable typography.

faqs.question: What is the Mobile Thumb Zone?
faqs.answer: The natural arc an adult thumb can easily reach while holding a smartphone with one hand; critical primary CTAs should be placed in the bottom center natural reach zone.

faqs.question: What is the minimum recommended touch target size for mobile UI?
faqs.answer: Apple HIG recommends a minimum touch target size of 44x44 points; Android Material Design recommends 48x48 dp.
